primitives.name: Trust Receipts
primitives.verbatim_quote: # GSN Feature Backlog Date: 2026-06-10 Scope: GSN / Galaxy Sports Edge sports intelligence only ## Trust Layer ### Feature Name Trust Receipts ### User Problem Users cannot tell whether a recommendation is based on current, high-quality sports intelligence or stale/fabricated confidence.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R(t)': 'Recommendation at time t, dimensionless', 'S(t)': 'Source freshness score at time t, [0,1]', 'U(t)': 'Uncertainty driver magnitude at time t, [0,1]', 'C(t)': 'Conflict state indicator at time t, {0,1}', 'M(t)': 'Model disagreement index at time t, [0,1]'}
primitives.assumptions: Recommendations are conditionally independent given receipt data; all variables are bounded in [0,1].
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R(t) lacks sufficient S(t), U(t), C(t), or M(t) values, trust degrades below threshold.

layer2.mapping: Each receipt maps to a conditional probability distribution P(R|D) where D represents the receipt data.
layer2.telemetry: Receipt completeness ratio, average confidence band width

primitives.name: Source Quality Meter
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Source Intelligence ### Feature Name Source Quality Meter ### User Problem Users need to understand why one report matters more than another when injury news, beat reports, market movement, and public social chatter conflict.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Q_s': 'Source quality score, [0,1]', 'P_s': 'Provenance score, [0,1]', 'F_s': 'Freshness score, [0,1]', 'I_s': 'Independence score, [0,1]', 'H_s': 'Historical correction rate, [0,1]', 'R_s': 'Incentive risk score, [0,1]'}
primitives.assumptions: Quality metrics are additive with diminishing returns; each metric is normalized to [0,1].
primitives.breakdown_regime: When H_s approaches 1, Q_s decays due to frequent corrections.

layer2.mapping: Q_s = w1*P_s + w2*F_s + w3*I_s + w4*H_s + w5*R_s, with weights summing to 1.
layer2.telemetry: Average source quality band, proportion of high-quality sources

primitives.name: Game State Summary
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### Product Behavior Game cards summarize line movement, injury/news volatility, sharp/public divergence, model disagreement, confidence decay, and recommended action.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L(t)': 'Market line at time t, currency units', 'V(t)': 'Volatility measure, [0,1]', 'D(t)': 'Sharp/public divergence, [0,1]', 'M(t)': 'Model disagreement index, [0,1]', 'C(t)': 'Confidence decay factor, [0,1]', 'A(t)': 'Recommended action, {Bet, Watch, NoBet}'}
primitives.assumptions: All dynamics are piecewise continuous; A(t) is a function of L(t), V(t), D(t), M(t), C(t).
primitives.breakdown_regime: When D(t) exceeds threshold, A(t) defaults to 'Watch'.

layer2.mapping: A(t) = argmax_{a} P(a | L(t), V(t), D(t), M(t), C(t))
layer2.telemetry: Action accuracy rate, average confidence decay per game

Trust receipts and source quality meters define a layered epistemic architecture. The receipt layer ensures transparency via bounded uncertainty quantification, while the source meter provides a scalar credibility metric. These primitives enable GSI to maintain a dynamic Bayesian network where each recommendation's trustworthiness is a function of its source quality and temporal freshness. The game state summary acts as a situational filter, applying these trust metrics to derive actionable outcomes. The interplay between these operators creates a closed-loop system where trust degradation triggers re-evaluation of source credibility and recommendation validity. Failure modes include receipt omission leading to unverifiable signals and poor source quality causing spurious confidence propagation. The system enforces a dual constraint: no signal without receipt, and no signal without verified source quality.
